'''Michał Misiurewicz''' (born 9 November 1948<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199708/bios.pdf |title=Biographies of Candidates 1997 |access-date=30 April 2023}}</ref>) is a Polish [[mathematician]]. He is known for his contributions to [[Dynamical system#Nonlinear dynamical systems and chaos|chaotic dynamical systems]] and [[Fractal|fractal geometry]], notably the [[Misiurewicz point]].

Misiurewicz participated in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] for Poland, winning a bronze medal in 1965 and a gold medal (with perfect score and special prize) in 1966.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=9939|title=International Mathematical Olympiad}}</ref> He earned his [[Doctorate]] from [[University of Warsaw]] under supervision of Bogdan Bojarski.

In 1990, he moved to the [[United States]], where he visited [[Northwestern University]] and [[Princeton University]], eventually settling down at [[Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis]] at Indianapolis, Indiana, where he currently is a professor.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Michal Misiurewicz|url=https://math.indianapolis.iu.edu/~mmisiure/|access-date=2020-10-26|website=math.indianapolis.iu.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Michal Misiurewicz: People: People Directory: School of Science: IUPUI|url=https://science.iupui.edu/people-directory/people/misiurewicz-michal.html|access-date=2020-10-26|website=School of Science|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-02-04.</ref>
